column1: # Pokémon Legends: Arceus on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Game Freak's engine on SDK 11.4.0; game.tsv and the shader tables are upstream's, checked by hand. 73 of its 12,851 shaders live only in Oodle Kraken GFPAK entries:
# the porter decodes them with the game's own decoder on the device (dmhost, DM_OODLE_JOB), so a port needs the device connected.
# On the Y700 (2026-10-30), docked and handheld, driven with DM_CTL: the opening (Arceus, the name, the fall), the beach with Laventon and the starters, the first walks.
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch: patches.py), GPU 11-14.6 ms at the beach; a 30-minute soak kept one
# process at a flat 1,307 MiB footprint with no audio underruns and no red log line. The washed-out picture it first had was the vertex outputs' Maxwell start values
# (gfx_vk_shader.c spv_vs_init). Local wireless trades stay offline (nn::ldn cut): Trading Post → Local Communication not checked yet.
# On the AYN Thor (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Adreno 740, Android 13, Turnip 27.0.0-R2, 2026-11-11), played by hand from the same save with both builds installed side by side:
# the build with the cut plays like fast-forward, about twice as fast; this one (no cut) plays at the Switch's pace. The game runs at its own 30.
# On the Y700 again (2026-11-11, Qualcomm driver, docked): the same 3 s stick hold (DM_CTL LUp~3.0) from the beach's first-control spot walked twice as far with the cut
# at 60 as with no cut at 30, and the cut pinned at 30 (DM_FPS_PIN=30) walked as far as no cut: the 2026-10-30 record of game time at real time was wrong. No cut: 33.3 ms, no red line.

# The game steps its time by a stored frame period, not by the clock (patches.py "frame_step"): on the Odin 3 (2026-11-10) the 60 fps cut alone ran everything at double
# speed, and the pause menu's 30 by host pacing (DM_FRAME_CAP_MODE=pace, which this profile had) could not be right at both rates. With game.tsv's fps_target the period
# follows the host's frame step, and the pause menu frame cap (hle_framecap.c) sets its hold: Off / 60 one vsync, 30 two
# 60 fps on the Odin 3 (2026-11-11) needs a GPU clock floor of 734 MHz or more: at the 160 MHz floor the Adreno governor lowers the clock while the game holds 30, and every
# trial back to 60 fails (1.2-2.0 vsyncs a frame). 832 MHz held it; set without root through the firmware PServerBinder service, else su (front_android.c gpu_floor_apply)
# (no env row for it any more: 832 MHz is the default floor's clock on the Odin 3, three quarters of the top one, and the pause menu's GPU clock floor row changes it)
